_meta.indication: Ga 68 PSMA-11 Injection is a radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for PET of PSMA-positive lesions in men with prostate cancer: with suspected metastasis who are candidates for initial definitive therapy, and with suspected recurrence based on elevated serum PSA level.

pivotal_trials.population: Patients with intermediate-to high-risk prostate carcinoma who are candidates for initial definitive therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Per patient sensitivity and specificity for pelvic nodal metastases by pathology reference standard
pivotal_trials.result: In 123 evaluable patients, patient-level sensitivity 47% (95% CI 29%, 65%) and specificity 90% (95% CI 84%, 96%); PPV 61% (41%, 81%)

pivotal_trials.population: Patients with biochemical recurrence of prostate carcinoma after definitive therapy with prostatectomy or radiotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Per patient and per region PPV for tumor by pathology reference standard
pivotal_trials.result: Of 210 evaluable patients, 192 (91%) were true positive in one or more regions against the composite reference standard (95% CI 88%, 95%)

key_safety: No serious adverse reactions were attributed to Ga 68 PSMA-11 Injection; the most commonly reported adverse reactions were nausea, diarrhea, and dizziness, each occurring at a rate of <1%.
target_moa: 68Ga-PSMA-11 is a peptide-based positron-emitting radiopharmaceutical that binds to prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA), a transmembrane protein overexpressed in most prostate cancers, enabling PET imaging.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting or other external consultation was needed for this NDA.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under standard review.

summary.text: NDA 212642 was submitted under the 505(b)(2) pathway for a new molecular entity, received September 6, 2019, and reviewed under standard (non-priority) review; it was not referred to an advisory committee and was approved December 1, 2020.

citations.quote: New drug application (NDA) 212642 and NDA 212643 for ^{68}\text{Ga}-PSMA-11 were submitted simultaneously under the 505(b)(2) pathway.

Your application for PSMA-11 Ga 68 Injection was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of a disease.
